_comment: Mutation testing for the core CLI. Non-blocking (break: null) — run via
`npm run test:mutation` to surface a real mutation score, not as a CI gate.
WHY A TARGETED SCOPE: mutating all of src/**/*.ts is ~7k mutants and takes
hours, which nobody runs. The `mutate` list below is the subset where a
SURVIVING mutant is a safety problem rather than a cosmetic one — anything
that deletes files, decides what is skipped, builds a filesystem path, or
executes third-party code:
src/repairCommand.ts       (260 mutants) `repair --apply --prune` DELETES
local files. A survivor here means the prune
set can be wrong (deleting a claimed file, or
silently keeping an orphan) with no test noticing.
src/downloadCheckpoint.ts   (33 mutants) decides which tables a resumed
download SKIPS. A survivor means a stale
checkpoint is accepted and files are never
downloaded while the run reports success —
silent data loss, the exact bug the fingerprint
check was added to fix.
src/FileUtils.ts           (262 mutants) builds every local path and does
every read/write/delete on disk. Survivors here
are wrong-file / wrong-directory bugs.
src/genericUtils.ts        (108 mutants) owns the INJ-1 `isSafePathComponent`
path-traversal guard that FileUtils, the download
pipeline and the docs generator all rely on, plus
the chunking used to cap request fan-out.
src/PluginManager.ts        (78 mutants) resolves and executes third-party
plugin code in-process; survivors are
arbitrary-code-execution-shaped.
TOTAL IN SCOPE: 741 mutants, ~11 min wall clock on a 10-core machine.
`concurrency` BELOW IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT, NOT A PERFORMANCE KNOB — see
the next paragraph before raising it. On a machine with fewer than ~10 cores,
lower it further rather than leaving it.
READ THE TIMEOUT COUNT BEFORE THE SCORE.
Stryker counts a TimedOut mutant as DETECTED, on the theory that a mutant which
hangs the suite was caught by it. In this package a timeout means almost nothing
of the sort, so every one of them is silently added to the numerator and the
score comes out OPTIMISTIC, not conservative. Read the run as a BAND: the top is
Stryker's own figure, the bottom is the same figure with every timeout counted as
a survivor. At the default concurrency (cores - 1, so 9 here) that band is far
too wide to quote from — genericUtils.ts measured [36.27%, 95.10%].
WHAT THE TIMEOUTS ACTUALLY ARE — measured, not inferred. Stryker derives every
mutant's allowance from a dry run it performs SOLO
(timeout = timeoutFactor * netTime + timeoutMS + timeOverheadMS, see
mutant-test-planner.js; under `perTest` netTime counts only the COVERING tests,
so a small pure function is budgeted at little more than the constants) and then
executes mutants N-at-a-time. The allowance therefore never accounts for the
contention the mutants actually run under, and the shortfall is charged to the
mutant as if it had hung. Re-running genericUtils.ts unchanged at --concurrency 1
moved 47 of its 60 timeouts to Killed and 2 to SURVIVED, leaving 11 timing out
both times: 105 identical mutants, identical budget, identical tests, band
[36.27%, 95.10%] -> [77.67%, 94.17%]. Note that Stryker's headline barely moved
(95.10 -> 94.17) — the reported number is nearly blind to the thing that destroys
the measurement underneath it. Two earlier explanations were tested and are
wrong: machine load (an idle box gave 26.6% against the loaded 26.5%) and the
budget (raising it to timeoutMS 30000 / timeoutFactor 3, ~2.7x the effective
allowance, gave 26.7%). Hence the defaults below; the lever is --concurrency.
Corroborating, so this is not a one-experiment conclusion: 0 of 203 timeouts in
a full run tripped Stryker's instrumented hit limit, which a loop through the
mutated statement must trip; and swapping to coverageAnalysis 'off' — 363 tests
per mutant instead of 18, twenty times the work against 1.65x the budget — left
the RATE almost unchanged (58.3% -> 55.6%) while churning which mutants timed
out (27 Timeout -> Killed, 22 Killed -> Timeout). A hang times out in every
configuration; these do not.
DELIBERATELY DEFERRED (measured, not forgotten): src/snClient.ts (733
mutants) and src/manifestBuilder.ts (738 mutants). Both are high value, but
together they triple the runtime to ~50 min, which pushes the run out of
"a developer will actually do this" territory. Widen by appending them to
`mutate` when there is time to triage ~200 more survivors.
